According to Overbeck's description (Overbeck P4, p. 273) the central painting depicted the competition between light gods.

9. Tablinum (4), wall E: the drawing by N. The Fox (cfr. Disegnatori, p. 707, fig. 168) reproduces the painting, also described by Helbig (H, 971), which is another of the replicas of the competition between the gods of light, judged by Dionysus with the long torch, and which was initially interpreted as a myth of Adonis. The standing woman, bejeweled and with a garland in her hands is Venus, the seated young man, covered by a green mantle, with the blue nimbus surmounted by a star and with the pedum at his feet, is Hesperus, two other nymbed female deities, two Yorito, watch the dispute from above. 22-23. Oecus (q): the floor retains evident signs of the organization of the environment before the changes in progress in 79 A.D. throughout the S part of the perstyle. The field was of mosaic with a white background with rows of large black tesserae and in the center there was a carpet of flakes of polychrome limestone and rhomboidal palombino tiles bedded in the background with white tesserae. It dates back to the first style while the decoration of the wall, which overlaps it, is of an initial III style that still has many reminiscences of the II, especially in the organization of the middle area.

24. Oecus (q): the structural articulation and details of the S wall were still quite evident until a few decades ago (cf. Bastet, cited in bibl., that in tav. III, 5 publishes an old photo) and it could be seen that in it there were still elements of the II style. The plinth had panels with plans separated from the bases and the lower part of the columns placed in front of the structure of the middle area. In this in the center there is the aedicule with a landscape painting, "purple oligochrome, green and blue", very high and which continues with the tympanum in the upper area; on the sides three panels on each side, alternating purple and red, with a column placed in the center that is connected by a short architrave to another placed at the back. Above the blue frieze intended as the sky, and "a row of rectangles lying with representations of birds on a black background", follows the upper area with architecture and pavilions, and the upper part of the aedicule with the tympanum surmounted by rectangular elements, to which a colonnaded hemicycle is the background. The lunette closes the wall with a still life scene with a rooster and a hen among pomegranates, facing right towards an altar on which they are offered; on the right there is an overturned basket from which fruit and grapes come out and on which a bird and a goose rest. The stucco frame that bordered the lunette is completely lost.  78 N45837
25. Oecus(q), S wall: detail of the lunette with still life. You can recognize the shelf on which the hen rests and, in the background, the rooster.

32. Room (z), wall E, section N: fresco of the fourth style of modest quality. The painting, now completely vanished, depicted the story of Ero and Leandro.

33. Room (z), wall E, section N: the edges of the volute carpet that delimit the white panel of the middle area are executed on a band of contrasting colour (red), as is usual in the 'popular' decorations of the Bottega dei Pittori in Via di Castricio (cf. De Vos, PRoma).

34. The painting in figure 32 represents the story of Leander, who will lose his life swimming at night across the arm of the sea that separates him from Hero, who is waiting for him here at the tower (H, 1374). The reproduction by G. Abbate is from 1841 (cfr. Disegnatori, pp. 282-283, fig. 74).

35. Room (z), S wall, with lunette: the wall decoration of the fourth style is very badly preserved, but what remains is sufficient to conclude that we are faced with a decoration of a very modest level, which nevertheless seeks, with a series of expedients that fit perfectly into the 'strategy' of the Painters' Workshop Via di Castricio,  to achieve a certain effect on the observer. The short wall is divided by a narrow compartment with a red background, in which is a vegetable candelabra. In the white side panels there are aedicules bordered by bands with carpet edges, in the center of which there were vanid squares.

36. Room (z), wall O, section S: red plinth with plants; white middle area with a panel bordered by a red band with carpet edges (arranged in such a way as to simulate a shrine seen in perspective) resting on corner volutes. A low candelabrum adorns the upper and lower parts of the panel, in the center of which was a painting now destroyed. The middle area ends with a stucco frame. IV style.

37. The panel reproduced in the previous figure depicted another story of unhappy love set on the shores of the sea, that of Ariadne's abandonment by Theseus (H, 1226), here reproduced from a panel by G. Abbate of 1841 (cf. Disegnatori, pp. 282-283, fig. 75).

Room (z), wall O, central section: between two red compartments crossed by vegetable candelabra surmounted by the globe, the panel is bordered by carpet edges whose arrangement suggests the presence of a shrine seen from the front. Inside the panel is a vanished medallion, in the pediment of the aedicule is a sphinx with open wings. IV style.

8. VII 5, 15. Cubicle (c): detail of the black and white mosaic floor now not visible because it was covered by a protective plank affixed to it as early as the 30s of this century, as the room was used by the excavation staff. It featured a combination of lozenges that formed eight-pointed stars, with squares in the resulting spaces, in each of which is a six-petaled corolla sometimes inscribed in a circle. In the marginal triangles resulting on the sides there was a motif of leaves with toothed margins describing a large U with outward-facing terminations.

9. VII5, 15. Cubicle (c), N wall, interrupted by a modern window: the black plinth is geometric, the panels in fact have concentric squares placed in the center by corner or simple and with a central cross, connected to the edges by perpendicular lines. The aedicule in the middle area has a yellow background and the side panels are separated by a narrow compartment with a black background crossed by a thin candelabra.

11. VII5, 15. Cubicle (c), wall E, section S: of the III style decoration in the antechamber remains part of the red panel of the middle area crossed by a thin pillar separating the alcove.

86. Pronaos (2): the plan and elevation taken by F. La Vega and engraved by C. Nolli restore, more than reality, the appearance of the temple building itself, at the time of the excavation. Apart from the stucco cladding of the façade, still discreetly preserved, with the presentation of motifs typical of the IV style, the mosaic flooring found was interesting, already largely destroyed, especially in the cella. In the pronaos there were checkerboard motifs in the intercolumns, and between the threshold of the staircase and the door of the cella, a carpet of four-pointed stars laced together; in the small room, frequented only by priests, there was finally a combination of fastened dodecagons with a star of six triangles and squares with Solomon's knots in the center of each, in the realization of which colored tiles had also been used and which was found already partly destroyed.
